//: Seven shapes, and each one is a shape from the corpus rather than a shape
from the grammar. `export def` never arrives without its `describe` block
— an exported definition MUST describe itself, checked both ways — so the
snippet brings both or it is teaching a refusal. The spray package brings
all three of its parts for the same reason: the fold, the pack and the
kernel share one file because that is what a package IS.
Bodies indent by four. Ruled 2026-09-09, and the printer emits four, so a
snippet that taught two would be wrong the first time anyone formats.

export def with describe.description: An exported definition and the describe block it is held to
body: ${2:rate}    "${8:What this parameter means, and what moves when you turn it.}"

def.description: A local definition — a private helper, flattened at parse

def on row.description: A definition that runs on the row plane — it may name row. and slate.

describe.description: A describe block for a definition already written

using.description: Bind a fold — tokens captured verbatim, spliced back at :name

also.description: Fan out inline — the same value down a side branch

spray package.description: A spray package: the room, the pack, the kernel — one file, three things
body: // ${1:name} — ${2:what this population looks like, in one line.}
// `@self` resolves to the SPRAY's name at mount, so two sprays of one
// The body is `0` on purpose: instantiating this would bake the defaults
// in as literals, and the numbers have to reach the kernel LIVE through
// the `.k.` room. `export def` is here for its PACK.
"${2:what this population looks like, in one line.}"
rate     "Rows born a second. With `life` this is the population budget — rate x life rows exist in the steady state, and it must fit under `capacity`."
speed    "Metres a second along the spray's aim, applied once at birth."
spread   "Per-axis random jitter added to the launch velocity, in +/- metres a second."
life     "How long a row lives, in MILLISECONDS. `perish` below is what reaps at it."
capacity "Rows allocated, for the population's whole life. Keep it above rate x life."
blend    "How the cards blend over the frame: `add` lights onto it, `alpha` lays over it."
// One program, run per row, per tick.
// Aim x speed + jitter, once, on the first tick of a row's life. Without
// this a row is born at rest and `speed` and `spread` do nothing.
// Retire the row on the first tick its age reaches its life. Marks only;
// the spray reaps in a serial phase. Without it, rows are immortal.
